pillars.The Stack: What the tools are and how they connect.
pillars.The Build: How a thing actually gets made, step by step.
pillars.The Standard: What 'good' means technically, with a number attached.
pillars.The Fix: A specific failure, its cause, and the repair.
pillars.The Tradeoff: Two valid options and how to choose.

coverRule: surface is ALWAYS light. These are the tiles that fill the feed's light slots.
editorialNote: The strongest topics here are the ones where Kymbo already has a written internal standard — a number we actually hold ourselves to beats a generic best practice. Those are marked source:'Notion'.

topics.title: The five layers of a hotel tech stack
topics.hook: Your hotel runs on 5 systems. Most owners can only name 2.
topics.angle: Name the layers, then land that the booking engine is the only one deciding who owns the guest.
proof: PMS · channel manager · booking engine · payments · CRM
hub-and-spoke: the PMS is the hub

topics.title: Which PMS for which property
topics.hook: Six systems. Pick wrong and you rebuild in 18 months.
topics.angle: Kymbo's actual vendor decision table, published. Boutique hotel → Cloudbeds or Mews. Under 20 rooms → Little Hotelier. Vacation rentals → Hostaway or Guesty. This is genuine expertise, not a listicle.

topics.title: What happens between 'Book now' and your inbox
topics.hook: Nine things happen in the 3 seconds after a guest hits Book.
topics.angle: Availability check → hold → payment authorization → PMS write → channel push → confirmation. Auth and capture are two different moments — that's the lesson.

topics.title: Two-way vs one-way sync (this is how double bookings happen)
topics.hook: One-way sync tells the OTA nothing. That's the bug.
topics.angle: The most expensive misconfiguration in small-property tech, in one diagram. Kymbo's own listed pitfall: 'inventory sync errors between PMS and OTAs (overbooking risk)'.
proof: proper channel manager integration drops overbookings 90%+

topics.title: Widget or full integration — how to choose
topics.hook: You don't always need a new website.
topics.angle: Kymbo's two tiers as a genuine decision tree. Widget = embedded booking engine, availability synced to the PMS calendar. Full integration = API-connected, real-time calendar + pricing sync, payment flow configured, staging-tested before go-live to prevent double-booking. Teach the difference; the sale follows.
proof: widget: real-time availability synced to the client's calendar
full: API-connected, staging tested before go-live

topics.title: WordPress vs headless: who owns your SEO output
topics.hook: Going headless silently breaks your schema. Here's why.
topics.angle: The real distinction isn't speed, it's which system emits the canonical, the sitemap and the JSON-LD. A headless migration is exactly where schema breaks without anyone noticing.
proof: WordPress owns content fields; the frontend owns URL, metadata, canonical, JSON-LD, sitemap, redirects

topics.title: The 5 schema types every hotel site needs
topics.hook: Schema is how AI search learns your hotel exists.
topics.angle: Kymbo's own SEO QA gate lists exactly five: Organization site-wide, Article on posts, LocalBusiness for hotels, Breadcrumb on inner pages, FAQPage where FAQs exist. Verify with Google's Rich Results Test — no errors, or the gate fails.

topics.title: The performance budget we hold every build to
topics.hook: LCP 2.5s. CLS 0.1. INP 200ms. Miss one, it doesn't ship.
topics.angle: Publish the actual internal gate. Nobody else in this market publishes numbers they're accountable to — that IS the authority play. Average hotel page is 6.3s against a 2.5s bar.
topics.source: Notion → WordPress Performance and Core Web Vitals

topics.title: LCP, INP, CLS — explained without the jargon
topics.hook: Three letters decide whether Google shows your hotel.
topics.angle: Define each by what the guest feels, then attach the threshold. INP matters most for a booking engine — date pickers are interaction-heavy.

topics.title: Plugin sprawl is why your site is slow
topics.hook: Max 15 plugins. 25 if you're on Elementor. That's the rule.
topics.angle: A hard number people can audit themselves this afternoon. Kymbo's stated position: plugin sprawl is the single biggest cause of slow WP sites, audited quarterly.
proof: Query Monitor + Plugin Performance Profiler to find the slow ones
topics.source: Notion → WordPress Performance and Core Web Vitals

topics.title: The image pipeline that costs you bookings
topics.hook: Your room photos are the reason the page is slow.
topics.angle: Hotels are photo-heavy by nature, so this is the highest-leverage speed fix for this audience specifically. The counter-intuitive bit: never lazy-load the hero — it gets eager + fetchpriority=high.
proof: compress before upload; WebP; lazy-load below fold only
width/height on every img or you get CLS
topics.source: Notion → WordPress Performance and Core Web Vitals

topics.title: Every third-party script costs you 50–200ms
topics.hook: That chat widget has a price. Here it is.
topics.angle: Reframes 'just add the pixel' as a budget decision. Kymbo's split: GA4 and Search Console required; Meta Pixel, Hotjar, Klaviyo, chat justified case-by-case; full-page A/B testing and generic chat rejected by default.
proof: all load via defer or interaction-triggered
topics.source: Notion → WordPress Performance and Core Web Vitals

topics.title: The five launch killers we check for every time
topics.hook: Five settings that quietly delete you from Google.
topics.angle: Straight from the SEO QA gate: 'Discourage search engines' left on, robots.txt Disallow:/ from staging, noindex left by a staging plugin, missing 301s on migration, leaked staging URLs. Cheap pre-launch, expensive after.

topics.title: Redirect chains are eating your migration
topics.hook: A → B → C is a bug. It should be A → C.
topics.angle: Narrow, concrete, and universally botched on redesigns — the exact moment a hotel loses its rankings.
proof: redirect list confirmed with the client

topics.title: Shared hosting is why it's slow, and we won't build on it
topics.hook: We reject GoDaddy and Bluehost. Here's the math.
topics.angle: A real, slightly spiky position with the tiering behind it: SiteGround for informational, Cloudways for control, Kinsta/WP Engine for traffic. Taking a stand is the whole point of this one.
proof: SiteGround budget · Cloudways mid · Kinsta/WP Engine premium
shared hosting rejected for any build
topics.source: Notion → WordPress Performance and Core Web Vitals § Hosting

topics.title: What caching actually caches
topics.hook: There are four caches. Most sites configure one.
topics.angle: Page, browser, object, CDN — four layers, four different jobs. Explains why 'I installed a cache plugin' doesn't fix a slow site.
proof: WP Rocket default, W3 Total Cache free alternative
combine plugin + host cache carefully or they conflict
topics.source: Notion → WordPress Performance and Core Web Vitals § Caching

topics.title: Google free booking links: zero commission, most hotels miss it
topics.hook: There's a free slot on Google labelled 'Official site'.
topics.angle: Genuinely actionable and under-used by independents. The connectivity-partner requirement is the part that stops people — that's the payoff slide.
proof: needs a connectivity partner sending live rates + availability
listed as 'Official site' under All options

topics.title: OTA, metasearch, direct — three different money models
topics.hook: Three ways a guest arrives. Three completely different bills.
topics.angle: Commission vs CPC vs free. Most owners treat all traffic as one thing; the pricing model is the whole story.

topics.title: Gateway, processor, merchant account — who's who
topics.hook: Three companies touch every card payment. You're paying all three.
topics.angle: Nobody explains this cleanly to small operators, and it's where hidden per-booking cost lives.
proof: Stripe / Adyen / regional are the usual PMS-side processors

topics.title: PCI basics for a property taking cards
topics.hook: If you email a card number, you own the breach.
topics.angle: Scope reduction is the lesson: hosted/tokenized fields collapse your PCI burden. Listed in Kymbo's own hospitality pitfalls as 'skipping payment provider compliance'.

topics.title: What a channel manager does when you change one rate
topics.hook: You change $10. Watch what fires.
topics.angle: Trace one edit across every connected surface. Makes an invisible system visible — the ideal diagram carousel.
proof: 30% less manual OTA management within a quarter

topics.title: Domain, DNS, hosting, CDN — the four people confuse
topics.hook: Your domain is not your hosting. This costs people weeks.
topics.angle: Foundational, evergreen, and the reason migrations and handoffs go wrong.

topics.title: A booking form without HTTPS is a dead form
topics.hook: One browser warning ends the booking.
topics.angle: Short, absolute, easy to verify — a good quick-hit between heavier carousels. Mixed content is the sneaky version.

topics.title: The 5-step booking flow that converts
topics.hook: Dates. Categories. Rates. Summary. Details. Nothing else.
topics.angle: Mirrors the flow in our own demo product, so the carousel doubles as a product demo without being an ad. Every extra step is an abandonment opportunity.

topics.title: Anatomy of a booking page that converts
topics.hook: Nine elements. Miss three and the page leaks.
topics.angle: Labelled teardown of our own demo product, annotated. Strongest device-composite candidate in the bank.

topics.title: The GA4 events that actually measure a booking funnel
topics.hook: Pageviews tell you nothing. Six events tell you everything.
topics.angle: Name the events and where each fires. Turns analytics from decoration into diagnosis. GA4 is a required install on every Kymbo build.

topics.title: How to read your booking engine's conversion rate
topics.hook: 2% doesn't mean anything until you know the denominator.
topics.angle: Sessions vs searches vs availability-found — three denominators, three wildly different numbers, and vendors quote whichever flatters them.

topics.title: GDPR for guest data, in five plain rules
topics.hook: You collected the email. Now you're responsible for it.
topics.angle: Consent, purpose limitation, retention, access, deletion — applied to a hotel CRM. Unsexy, high-trust, very shareable with owners.

topics.title: Staging, backups, uptime — the boring stuff that saves you
topics.hook: The worst time to learn you have no backup is Friday.
topics.angle: Three cheap insurances and the cost of skipping each. This is literally what the Care Plan buys — teach it, don't pitch it.
proof: core/plugin updates, security, backups, uptime monitoring
monthly health report pulled directly from the host

topics.title: Why we test the payment flow on staging before go-live
topics.hook: The first real booking is the worst place to find the bug.
topics.angle: Explains a line most clients skim past in the scope. The failure it prevents — a double booking on a live calendar — is vivid and specific.
proof: staging tested before go-live to prevent double-booking

topics.title: Elementor or custom theme — the honest comparison
topics.hook: Elementor ships with jQuery. Sometimes that's fine.
topics.angle: Kymbo runs both paths, so the comparison is credible rather than dogmatic: template speed vs long-term control, and the plugin ceiling that comes with each.
proof: custom theme: vanilla ES2020+, no jQuery
topics.source: Notion → Elementor with Envato; WordPress Performance

topics.title: The database maintenance nobody does
topics.hook: Your site stores every draft you ever wrote. Forever.
topics.angle: Tiny, actionable, surprising: WP_POST_REVISIONS = 5, clean transients, OPTIMIZE TABLE. One line in wp-config that most sites never get.
topics.source: Notion → WordPress Performance and Core Web Vitals § Database
